subject: treasureHoard
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: treasure hoard: coins, gems, chest, crown, goblets.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static treasure prop without joints, building out the chest, coin pile, gems, crown, and goblets using the part/lathe/extrude builder methods with metallic paints and glow textures.

For the chest, I'm placing it at the back center with an open lid built as a half-cylinder geometry, translated so its hinge sits at the back top edge, then rotated to tilt back around 110 degrees open.

Reconsidering the cylinder orientation, I decide a cleaner approach is extruding a half-disc profile for the lid in the local hinge plane, then rotating that 2D outline to represent the open angle before extruding it along the chest's width.

For the gold bands lining the lid, I'll extrude the same profile scaled up slightly with thin thickness positioned along the edges. For the chest body itself, I'm planning a wooden box with gold band accents, corner reinforcements, a lock plate with a glowing gem, and a pile of coins inside.

For the coin pile, I want a flattened conical mound of overflowing gold at the top with individual coins scattered on its surface, plus a few coin stacks nearby. To keep the part count manageable I'll merge all the coin cylinder geometries into a single mesh using a geometry-merging utility, building each coin's transform matrix and combining them by color group rather than treating each as a separate part.

For gems, I'm using low-poly octahedrons and icosahedrons with glow effects and varied colors scattered across the pile. The crown gets a lathe-profile band with cone spikes topped by small spheres and gems embedded in the band, sitting on the mound. Goblets use a lathe profile for foot, stem, and bowl, gold-colored with gems, with one tipped over for variety. I'm leaning into a hextech-style aesthetic with glowing blue gem accents on the lock plate and crown, plus adding a crest decal on the chest front and an embossed texture on a few hero coins for extra detail.

I'll keep it to three textures total: the crest, a wood-grain paint pattern, and a coin emblem applied to a few standing coins leaning against the pile rather than full geometry planes. For coloring, wood uses noise-based grain streaks while gold gets a mottled look mixing dark and light tones with countershading. The mound itself is built from a lathe profile with points tracing the outer curve from the base up to the peak, closing back along the central axis.

Now I'm working out the coin pile placement relative to the chest—figuring the chest's depth and lid opening angle so the pile sits naturally in front, with a height function approximating the mound's curve for scattering coins at random radii, angles, and slight tilts in varying gold shades. I'm also planning a smaller interior mound inside the chest itself, along with scattered gems, and setting the solid chest body dimensions.

Checking that overall model height works out with the lid open, then defining a gem helper that builds faceted icosahedron shapes with a subtle glow, resting them properly on the mound surface. Now I'm positioning a crown off to the side on the mound, calculating its radial distance from the pile center to get the right height offset before building its band shape locally and placing it with a slight tilt.

Designing the crown's band, spikes, and gem accents, then moving on to sketching a lathe profile for the goblets with inner and outer shell walls.

I'm positioning the tipped goblet lying on its side near the mound edge with coins spilling from its mouth, then considering adding coin stacks and a hero coin with an emblem texture on the floor.

Writing gold paint function...

I'll import mergeGeometries for combining the coin geometries. For the chest, I'm planning a shield-and-crown crest decal on the front, plus gold strap bands running vertically on the sides and trim boxes along the top and bottom edges, adjusting their dimensions so they don't overlap the body's interior mound.

Instead I'll build the top trim as a frame made of four separate rim boxes rather than one solid piece, with corner studs added as small spheres. For the lid, I'm adding matching gold bands and an outline extrusion over the wood base, plus a front lock hasp plate positioned above the crest without overlapping it.

Now I'm adding a glowing cyan octahedron gem inside the lock for a hextech feel, computing the outline rotation around the proper axis, and starting to write the generator code with a seeded RNG function.
